name: manual_94cbd6
claim: When 'gh'/'git push' auth fails with 'Invalid username or token', check for a stale env var matching the CLI's exact lookup name (gh reads GH_TOKEN first, then GITHUB_TOKEN; Git uses GITHUB_TOKEN only when its configured credential helper, e.g. one installed by 'gh auth setup-git', reads it) before assuming the stored credential is broken -- check both GH_TOKEN and GITHUB_TOKEN, since GH_TOKEN takes precedence; 'gh auth status' with the shadowing var unset reveals whether a working keyring-stored token is being shadowed; scope the fix to 'env -u <shadowing var> <cmd>' (GH_TOKEN and/or GITHUB_TOKEN) per-command rather than editing the secrets file that defines it.

decisions.notes: ~/.env defines a stale/invalid GITHUB_TOKEN that gh CLI (and git, via a gh-installed credential helper) check before their keyring-stored credential, so every push attempted 'normally' failed with 'Authentication failed', even though 'gh auth status' showed a valid, active diazMelgarejo keyring token underneath it. Same shape as the earlier GITHUB_PERSONAL_ACCESS_TOKEN-vs-CODEX_GITHUB_PERSONAL_ACCESS_TOKEN naming mismatch found this same session on the MCP github plugin: an env var with the exact name a tool checks silently overrides a working credential, and the fix is scoping/unsetting per-invocation, never guessing or rewriting the secrets file blind.
